via-crucis-a-romance-of-the-second-crusa: F. Marion Crawford sets this sweeping historical romance during the Second Crusade of 1147. Knights, pilgrims, and princes march toward the Holy Land through a story of faith tested by love and war. Crawford, a master of the popular historical novel, fills the march east with vivid battles and a tender love story at its heart.
aikenside: Mary Jane Holmes — one of America's most popular novelists — tells a domestic story of love, misunderstanding, and reconciliation at Aikenside. Her millions of readers loved her warm, moral romances of home and heart. Victorian popular fiction at its most beloved and comforting.
life-at-high-tide: William Dean Howells pictures life at high tide — American prosperity and its discontents in stories of quiet power. His realism finds drama in the everyday. Subtle, humane fiction. His quiet people face modern America with dignity and doubt. Prosperity's tide lifts his characters, then tests them.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adelaide: This 1913 reference article on Adelaide — the Australian archdiocese of the south. Henry Cleary traces its growth. Irish settlers built its churches. The city of churches earned its name. A young Church in an old land. Its cathedral honors St. Francis Xavier.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-albert-of-sta: This 1913 reference piece on Albert of Stade — the chronicler of the northern annals. Thomas Shahan follows his record. His chronicle runs to 1264. The Hanse towns live in his pages. A monk's view of the German north. His annals end with the interregnum.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-side: This 1913 reference article on the altar's sides — epistle and gospel ends. Augustin Schulte explains the old names. The deacon reads from the north. The subdeacon sings from the south. The altar's twofold service. Their names survive in the old missals.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-averbode: A 1913 entry on Averbode — the Premonstratensian abbey of Brabant. Michael Ott notes its white canons. Its press serves the order's cause. The Revolution spared its walls. A jewel of the Norbertines. Its library serves the learned canons. Its canons wear the white habit.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bede: This 1913 reference article on the Venerable Bede — the father of English history. Herbert Thurston honors his Jarrow cell. His Ecclesiastical History lit the dark age. The scholars bless his toil. England's first great scholar. His deathbed song is famed. His relics rest in Durham's shrine.
